question.text: Tungabhadra Buyout II (Cat II): Committed INR 200 cr (fully called). Terminal NAV INR 330 cr. Hurdle 8% compounded. 5-yr tenure. Carry 20% WITHOUT catch-up. Compute the residual profit (above hurdle) and the GP carry.

answer.text: Residual INR 36.1 cr; GP carry INR 7.22 cr
Residual INR 130.0 cr; GP carry INR 26.0 cr
Residual INR 46.9 cr; GP carry INR 26.0 cr
Residual INR 36.1 cr; GP carry INR 26.0 cr

explanation.text: The Logic: Compounded hurdle at year 5: INR 200 x (1.08)^5 = INR 293.87 cr, so the hurdle return is INR 93.87 cr. Total profit = INR 330 - 200 = INR 130 cr. Residual above hurdle = INR 130 - 93.87 = INR 36.13 cr. With NO catch-up, the GP receives 20% of the residual = 20% x INR 36.13 = INR 7.23 crore. The Trap: Option B ignores the hurdle entirely and applies 20% to total profit. Option C uses a wrong residual base. Option D combines the correct residual with an incorrect carry computation. Note: The no-catch-up waterfall here matches Example 6.5 in the source; the GP earns carry only on the above-hurdle slug.
